newsitem.title: HONG KONG: U.S. stock losses dent Asian markets for 2nd day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock losses dent Asian markets for 2nd day.

text.p: An overnight slide on Wall Street slammed Asian markets again on Friday, with Tokyo falling 2.5 percent in early trade before rebounding and Hong Kong shares down by more than two percent at the close.

U.S. blue chips plunged in the last hour of trading on Thursday, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell nearly 100 points in its biggest point loss since mid-July. It shed 1.54 percent to close at 6,303.71.
U.S. traders said a wave of computer-driven sell orders swamped the market in late trading. Stocks also came under pressure as a rally in the U.S. bond market withered.
Asian markets followed the Dow's lead early, except for Taiwan, which remained in positive territory until late morning.
The sharp drop on Wall Street overnight cast a shadow over Japan shares, which tumbled in choppy trading.

The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares briefly fell more than 500 points, or 2.5 percent, in hectic morning trade to about 19,987. It was the first time the index had been below the key 20,000 level in three months.
But the index managed to claw back above the 20,000 mark at the close to end the day at 20,341.39, a loss of 159.81 points or 0.78 percent.
"Due to the New York sell-off, we can't hope for foreign investors' buying in Tokyo. That dampened the Nikkei average," said Harushige Kobayashi, deputy general manager at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index sagged 2.06 percent or 269.21 points to finish at 12,784.07.
Selling was driven by overseas investors, nervous about international equity market trends, brokers said.
"It's a bit unsettling what is happening overseas," said Archie Hart, sales director at BZW Securities. "But Hong Kong has been quite resilient compared to other markets."
The Australian share market also back-pedalled sharply, losing 0.99 percent or 23.1 points to end at 2316.5.
New Zealand share prices however, fared slightly better. The NZSE-40 Capital Index ended 12.60 points, or 0.53 percent down, at 2,349.91.
Malaysian stocks slid in thin trading, dragged down by the Dow's woes. At about 0850 GMT, the Composite Index was down 12.08 points, or 1.01 percent, at 1,187.61.
Jakarta's Composite Index was down 3.52 points, or 0.56 percent, to 624.38 points at 0850 GMT.
The Singapore stock market drifted lower in early trade but dealers said extremely thin volumes limited the downside.
At 0850 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was down 8.80 points at 2,173.75.
Thai stocks fell early as investors sold large capitalised stocks on Wall Street's cue, but the market recovered later. At 0850 GMT, the SET index had dipped 1.50 points to 870.75.
Seoul stocks sank to their second three-year closing low in as many days. But the market finished well off its intra-day low, helped by bargain-hunting late in the day, brokers said.
The composite index lost 0.31 of a point to 689.07.
Philippine shares weathered Wall Street's misery relatively well. At about 0900 GMT, the composite index was down 8.91 points, or 0.28 percent, to 3,120.20 points.
For most of Taiwan's session, share prices defied the trend. But late selling trimmed early gains, sending the index down 0.52 of a point to close at 6,825.10.
